description: Envoy proxy monitoring Dashboard with service level templates. Adapted from Envoy Gateway (Apache-2.0, https://github.com/envoyproxy/gateway); modified. See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

panels.description: Envoy proxies reporting live now. Zero means no data plane is serving; compare with the number of proxy pods you expect.
panels.title: Live servers

panels.description: Average time the proxies have been running. A value that keeps resetting is a crash loop or repeated restarts: read the proxy pods' events.
panels.title: Avg uptime per node

panels.description: Envoy heap memory reserved from the operating system, per proxy. Compare with the pod's memory limit.
panels.title: Heap Size

panels.description: Envoy heap memory in use, per proxy. Compare with the pod's memory limit; a steady climb is a leak or a growing configuration.
panels.title: Allocated Memory
Downstream RPS
panels.description: HTTP requests per second received by all proxies. The traffic level the rest of the dashboard is read against; a fall to zero with no cause is an outage upstream of the gateway.

panels.title: Downstream CPS
panels.description: New client connections per second, by proxy namespace. A spike is a client reconnecting in a loop or a connection-per-request client.

panels.title: Downstream Latency
panels.description: Client-facing request latency at p50, p90 and p99, in milliseconds. A rising p99 with a flat p50 is a slow backend or a saturated proxy.

panels.title: Downstream Total Connections
panels.description: Client connections open on the listeners, by proxy namespace. A steady climb is clients not closing connections.

panels.title: TCP Downstream CPS
panels.description: New TCP client connections per second on TCP routes, by proxy namespace.

panels.title: TCP Downstream Bytes Rx/second
panels.description: Bytes per second received from clients on TCP routes.

panels.title: TCP Downstream Bytes Tx/Second
panels.description: Bytes per second sent to clients on TCP routes.
Displays the number of Requests per Second being performed against each Upstream.
panels.title: Upstream RPS
Upstream CPS
panels.description: New connections per second from the proxies to backends, by proxy namespace. High churn with low request rate means connections are not reused.
Backend request latency at p50, p90 and p99, in milliseconds. Compare with the downstream latency to see how much time the backend accounts for.
panels.title: Upstream Latency
Upstream Total Connections
panels.description: Connections open from the proxies to backends, by proxy namespace. A steady climb is a backend not closing idle connections.
Bytes per second received from backends.
panels.title: Upstream Bytes Rx/Second
Upstream Bytes Tx/Second
panels.description: Bytes per second sent to backends.
Backend responses per second with a 2xx status. The healthy baseline the error panels are read against.
panels.title: Upstream 2xx Responses

panels.description: Backend responses per second with a 3xx status (redirects).
panels.title: Upstream 3xx Responses

panels.description: Backend responses per second with a 4xx status. A rise is clients sending bad requests or a broken route or auth policy.
panels.title: Upstream 4xx Responses

panels.description: Backend responses per second with a 5xx status. Should be near zero. A rise is a failing backend: open the Envoy clusters dashboard to see which one.
panels.title: Upstream 5xx Responses

panels.description: Healthy endpoints as a share of all endpoints known to the proxies, by proxy namespace. Below 100% means backends are failing health checks or being removed.
panels.title: Endpoint Percentage Health

panels.description: Backend endpoints known to the proxies, by proxy namespace.
panels.title: Total Endpoints

panels.description: Backend endpoints currently healthy, by proxy namespace.
panels.title: Healthy Endpoints

panels.description: Backend endpoints known to the proxies but not healthy, by proxy namespace. Should be zero; find them in the Envoy clusters dashboard.
panels.title: Unhealthy Endpoints
TLS Certificate Expiry
panels.description: Days until each certificate served by the listeners expires. Under 14 days and not renewing means cert-manager or the issuer is failing: open the cert-manager dashboard.
